Triveni Engineering & Industries: Guidance - - Concall Update

• Management provided a positive outlook for Q1 FY27, noting it was better than expectations, and anticipates a good Q2, with a significantly better operating season for the Sugar business in Q3 and Q4 FY27.

• For the Sugar business, the industry outlook remains constructive in the near-to-medium term, with excellent sugar pricing expected to be maintained going forward.

• In the Distillery business, the medium-term outlook is encouraging, with management anticipating a substantial amount of ethanol from grain next year, projecting a 3:1 grain to sugary feedstock ratio.

• Management expects to achieve operating plans for the Water business for the full year, despite slower Q1 execution, and sees a viable pipeline with expectations to be L1 in some bids.

• The Board is actively examining capital allocation for future growth, noting that while the Water business has an excellent business, its return on capital employed is not ideal, and the Country Liquor business has good return metrics but limited capital requirements and geographic constraints.

WAAREE Energies: Guidance - - Concall Update

• Management reaffirmed its operating EBITDA guidance of INR7,000 crores to INR7,700 crores for FY27, citing strong demand tailwinds, a record order book, and on-schedule expansion projects.

• The company projects its retail business to achieve INR9,000 crores to INR10,000 crores in revenue for the full year FY27.

• The announced CapEx program totals approximately INR31,500 crores, with INR9,450 crores deployed by June 30, and is phased with 30% in FY27, 40% in FY28, and 30% in FY29.

• Cell production is expected to ramp up sharply from 800 megawatts in Q1 FY27 to 1.2 gigawatts in Q2, 1.5 gigawatts in Q3, and over that in Q4, with module capacity utilization reaching 70% to 75% in Q3 and Q4.

• The company anticipates its cell-to-module integration ratio to increase from approximately 20% currently to around 65% in the next two to three quarters, significantly enhancing profitability.

Piramal Pharma: Guidance - - Concall Update

• Management reaffirmed the original full-year guidance for the CDMO business, noting that historically, higher revenues are delivered in H2, and they started Q1 with a stronger opening order book.

• They are not revising any guidance at this early stage, but may provide an update after the September quarter results.

• For the Complex Hospital Generics business, the full-year guidance is reaffirmed, encompassing both organic growth and Kenalog-related growth, though the Q1 organic growth rate is not expected to continue for the entire year.

• The normalized effective tax rate is expected to be in the range of 24% to 25% when the company is at scale, but it will remain elevated in the current fiscal year.

• Annual CapEx guidance is between $120 million to $135 million, with $21 million spent in Q1, and the Lexington CapEx is on track for completion by the end of calendar year 2027.

NUVAMA WEALTH Q1: BUSINESS HIGHLIGHTS 📊💼

• 💰 Wealth Management revenue rose 19% YoY to ₹447 Cr, while PBT increased 20% YoY to ₹149 Cr. Client assets grew 12% YoY to ₹3.64 lakh Cr.

• 📈 Nuvama Wealth revenue grew 13% YoY to ₹250 Cr. MPIS net inflows hit a record ₹3,044 Cr, with MPIS assets surging 32% YoY to ₹42,795 Cr.

• 🌟 Nuvama Private revenue increased 27% YoY to ₹198 Cr, with PBT up 22% YoY to ₹59 Cr. Underlying ARR net inflows remained healthy at ~₹1,800 Cr.

• 🏦 Asset Management fees rose 24% YoY to ₹22 Cr. Closing AUM grew 12% YoY to ₹13,261 Cr. Received SEBI's final Mutual Fund licence approval and initiated SIF launch process.

• 🤝 Asset Services & Capital Markets: Asset Services revenue grew 34% YoY, while segment PBT increased 19% YoY to ₹269 Cr. Client assets under Asset Services climbed 25% YoY to ₹1.59 lakh Cr.

NUVAMA WEALTH ; Management says Reported its highest-ever quarterly profit, with PAT exceeding ₹300 crore, revenue crossing ₹900 crore, and client assets surpassing ₹5 lakh crore.

• 💰 Wealth Management delivered strong growth, driven by healthy client additions, net inflows and stable margins, while continuing investments in talent and technology.

• 🤖 Saw encouraging progress in offshore wealth and AI-enabled productivity tools, strengthening future growth capabilities.

• 🏦 Asset Management achieved key milestones with the Mutual Fund licence approval and the successful close of its commercial real estate fund.

• 📊 Asset Services posted strong revenue growth through new mandates and deeper client engagement, while Capital Markets remained resilient despite market volatility.

• 🎯 Management reiterated its strategy of investing in organic growth, technology, AI, deeper client relationships and disciplined capital allocation to build a stronger long-term franchise.

INDEGENE Q1: MANAGEMENT Says Started FY27 strongly with 2.5% QoQ USD revenue growth, the strongest first-quarter sequential growth in four years.

• 🌍 Revenue grew 39.7% YoY (₹ terms) and 26.5% YoY (USD), while the active client base increased to 105, up by 14 sequentially.

• 🤝 Deepened customer relationships with 12 clients generating over $10 million in annual revenue each.

• ⚙️ Productivity improved, with revenue per employee rising to $77,000, the highest among peers.

• 🤖 Continued investing in GenAI-powered products, solutions and technologies to accelerate AI-driven life sciences commercialization.

• 📊 EBITDA and PAT margins improved sequentially, with management expecting higher operating leverage and stronger profitability in H2 FY27 as investments mature.

VEDANTA: APPROVES DEMERGER OF REAL ESTATE BUSINESS TO UNLOCK VALUE

Vedanta Ltd. has approved the demerger of its Real Estate Business into a separate entity, Vedanta Property Platforms Ltd. (VPPL), subject to regulatory and NCLT approvals.

Shareholders will receive 1 equity share of Vedanta Property Platforms Ltd. (FV ₹1) for every 20 equity shares of Vedanta Ltd. (FV ₹1) held on the record date, which will be announced later.

The demerged portfolio comprises around 2,200 acres of industrial land and approximately 55,000 sq. ft. of residential/commercial properties across India.

The move aims to unlock the value of Vedanta's non-core real estate assets, create a dedicated real estate platform, improve management focus, and attract sector-specific investors and strategic partners.

Vedanta will now seek stock exchange, SEBI, NCLT and other regulatory approvals before the scheme becomes effective.

*Impact: Positive* – The proposed demerger is expected to unlock the value of Vedanta's surplus real estate assets, improve business focus and transparency, and provide shareholders with direct ownership in a dedicated real estate platform.

• 🇮🇳 Swiggy's Board approved a proposal to cap foreign shareholding at 49.5%, paving the way to become an Indian Owned and Controlled Company (IOCC).

• ✅ As of July 1, 2026, domestic ownership crossed 50%, marking a key milestone in Swiggy's IOCC journey.

• 🛒 IOCC status will allow Instamart to directly own and sell inventory, in addition to its marketplace model, improving operational flexibility.

• 📈 Management expects the inventory-led model to improve Contribution Margin by ~80 bps, while providing better control over day-to-day operations.

• 🗳️ The proposal is subject to shareholder approval at the AGM on August 18, 2026, with the transition expected to be completed over the next 2–4 quarters.

• 🔄 Swiggy expects no disruption to customers or supplier relationships during the transition.

SWIGGY Q1 : Swiggy currently operates 1,171 dark stores across 131 cities, with ~40% store utilisation, providing significant room for growth within the existing network.

 The company plans to add ~75 new dark stores in Q2 FY27, primarily in high-growth neighbourhoods to support rising demand.

SWIGGY Q1: 'SWITCH TO BETTER' STRATEGY TO DRIVE NEXT PHASE OF QUICK COMMERCE GROWTH 🛒✨

• 🛍️ Swiggy believes the next competitive edge in quick commerce is curated assortment, rather than just faster delivery or a larger product catalogue.

• ⭐ Under its "Switch to Better" strategy, the company is expanding Noice private-label products and partnering with leading brands to offer high-quality, value-for-money alternatives.

• 🍽️ Focus categories include high-protein foods, premium home & kitchen products, and non-toxic toys, addressing evolving consumer preferences.

• 👥 Customers purchasing "Switch to Better" products have shown 30% higher retention than other customer cohorts.

• 📈 Management expects this curation-led, higher-margin strategy to create a sustainable competitive advantage and strengthen profitability in an increasingly commoditized quick commerce market.

SWIGGY Q1: QUICK COMMERCE GROWTH & PROFITABILITY ROADMAP 🚀📦

• 👥 Swiggy removed 4M+ unprofitable users/orders over the last three quarters, strengthening unit economics while improving customer experience.

• 📈 Early growth recovery is visible, with 4-week NOV growth improving to 10% (vs 1% in the previous four weeks) and 1-month user retention rising to 61% (from 55% YoY).

• 🎯 Management expects Contribution Margin to remain between 0% and -1% over the next few quarters while accelerating growth without compromising fiscal discipline.

• 💰 Swiggy targets Adjusted EBITDA break-even at an annualized ₹60,000 Cr NOV run-rate, with 25–30 Cr orders/quarter and 5–6% Contribution Margin.

• ⚙️ Key profitability drivers include higher-margin product mix (+₹10/order), advertising revenue (+₹10/order), store automation & densification (+₹5/order) and operating leverage (+₹5/order).

• 📦 Inventory-led operations could add another ₹4–5 per order, helping achieve profitability faster. Management reiterated its long-term ambition of ₹1 lakh Cr+ NOV with 4–5% Adjusted EBITDA margin.

SWIGGY Q1: QUICK COMMERCE HITS CONTRIBUTION BREAK-EVEN 🎯⚡

• ✅ Swiggy achieved Contribution Margin break-even in Q1FY27, meeting the target set five quarters ago despite intense competition.

• 💰 Contribution improved by ₹28 per order over the last five quarters, while Adjusted Revenue per Order (RPO) increased from ₹83 to ₹108.

• 📦 Strategy focused on better monetisation, larger basket sizes, wider assortment, non-grocery expansion, higher advertising revenue and operating leverage.

• 📉 Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed by ₹80 crore QoQ, reflecting improving unit economics.

• 🏪 Over 45% of dark stores turned Contribution Margin positive, up from 30% in the previous quarter.

• 🌆 5 of the top 7 cities became Contribution Margin positive, with 25% of the store network delivering 3–5% Contribution Margins.

SWIGGY Q1: CONFIDENT ON FOOD DELIVERY LEADERSHIP 🍔🚀

• 🛡️ Management sees no near-term threat from potential new entrants and remains confident in its food delivery growth trajectory.

• ⚙️ Swiggy believes its large restaurant network, technology platform and delivery infrastructure provide a significant cost advantage over new competitors.

• ⚡ Speed & Convenience: Bolt is now live in 700+ cities, while One BLCK caters to premium convenience-focused users.

• 🥗 Targeted Selection: Eat Right (High Protein, Low Sugar, Low Cal) contributes ~15% of food delivery volumes, alongside Desk Eats, Late Night Eats and Food on Train.

• 💸 Affordability: 99 Store and the standalone Toing app are expanding the addressable market by targeting value-conscious consumers.

• 🎯 Management says its "Speed, Selection & Affordability" strategy positions Swiggy well to defend market leadership while expanding the overall market.

SWIGGY Q1: FOOD DELIVERY OUTLOOK & MARGIN UPDATE 🍔📈

• 🍽️ Food Delivery GOV grew 17.4% YoY to ₹9,490 Cr; adjusted growth would have been ~18% excluding LPG-related restaurant cancellations.

• 💸 Value offerings gained traction, with 99 Store and Toing helping attract price-conscious users and expand category demand.

• 👥 User base remained strong with 17.8% YoY MTU growth, while basket value increased 4.8% YoY.

• 🎯 Management reiterated 18–20% Food Delivery GOV growth guidance (excluding Toing), supported by healthy user additions and affordability initiatives.

• 📉 Contribution & Adjusted EBITDA margins dipped 20 bps QoQ due to seasonal delivery partner investments and annual salary hikes.

• 📊 Despite seasonal pressure, Adjusted EBITDA margin improved 70 bps YoY, with management maintaining its medium-term 5% Adjusted EBITDA/GOV margin target.

THERMAX: BOARD APPROVES INTERNAL RESTRUCTURING SCHEME 🔄🏭

• 🏢 Board approved a Scheme of Arrangement & Amalgamation involving wholly-owned subsidiaries Thermax Bioenergy Solutions (TBSPL) and Thermax Cooling Solutions (TCSL) with Thermax Ltd.

• 🔄 Bioenergy EPC business of TBSPL will be demerged into Thermax Ltd, while TCSL will be amalgamated into Thermax Ltd.

• 📈 Move aims to simplify the group structure, reduce administrative overheads, improve operational efficiency and strengthen financial metrics.

• 💰 Management expects annual cost savings, better capital allocation and enhanced long-term shareholder value.

• 📌 No new shares will be issued, no change in Thermax's shareholding pattern, as both entities are wholly owned subsidiaries.

• ⚖️ Scheme is subject to NCLT and other statutory/regulatory approvals.

🟢 Impact: Positive (Internal restructuring should improve operational efficiency, reduce costs and strengthen the company's long-term business structure.)

HYUNDAI Q1: AI INTEGRATION ACROSS VALUE CHAIN TO DRIVE NEXT PHASE OF GROWTH 🤖🚗

• 🤖 Hyundai is embedding AI across its entire value chain, positioning AI as an intelligent co-worker to improve productivity and accelerate growth.

• 🛍️ Sales & Marketing: AI-powered sales agent, "HyGenie" GenAI chatbot and AI platform for vehicle promotions.

• 🏭 Manufacturing & Supply Chain: AI-driven quality inspection, predictive maintenance, production planning, inventory optimization and AI-based safety monitoring.

• 🔧 Service: AI-based customer support, service automation, voice-of-customer analytics and technician training & coaching.

• 🚘 Products: Focus on in-vehicle AI, natural voice interaction, conversational AI and personalized proactive assistance.

HYUNDAI Q1: SUPPLIER FIRE & EXPORT WEAKNESS IMPACT VOLUMES 🚗📉

• 🚘 Total sales declined 1.3% YoY to 1,78,082 units, impacted by the June supplier fire incident and geopolitical disruptions.

• 🇮🇳 Domestic sales grew 5.4% YoY to 1,39,374 units, while exports fell 19.6% YoY to 38,708 units.

• 🚙 SUVs remained the key growth driver, accounting for 70% of domestic sales, up from 69% a year ago.

• ⛽ Fuel mix remained stable with Petrol (64%), Diesel (17%), CNG (18%), and EV (1%).

• 🔥 Management expects 100% production normalization, healthy demand and new launches to support recovery from Q2 FY27.

• 🎯 Company reaffirmed FY27 guidance of 8–10% YoY volume growth (domestic & exports) and 11–14% EBITDA margin.

MANKIND PHARMA Q1: CONSUMER HEALTH & EXPORTS MAINTAIN GROWTH 🌍💊

• 🛍️ Consumer Healthcare revenue grew 4% YoY, impacted by the base effect of the discontinued cash-and-carry business.

• 📈 Gained market share in key brands including Manforce, Preganews and Gas-o-fast despite softer revenue growth.

• 📱 Modern Trade & E-commerce contribution increased to 15% (vs 11% last year), driven by 38% growth.

• 🚀 Secondary sales remained strong with Gas-o-fast (+10%) and Ova News (+36%) YoY growth.

• 🌍 International business revenue surged 29% YoY, reflecting strong export momentum.

• 🇺🇸 Mankind (excluding BSV) launched 1 new product in the US during Q1, taking the total US product launches to 49.

MANKIND PHARMA Q1: CHRONIC & SPECIALTY BUSINESSES DRIVE DOMESTIC GROWTH 💊📈

• 🇮🇳 Domestic business (excluding Consumer Health) grew 11% YoY, led by strong growth in Mankind and BSV specialty businesses.

• 📊 Secondary sales grew 12.7%, nearly matching Indian Pharma Market (IPM) growth of 13%.

• ❤️ Chronic therapies remained the key growth driver with Cardiac (+19.4%) and Anti-Diabetes (+12.7%).

• 🩺 Acute business recovered, supported by outperformance in Gastro (1.2x), VMN (1.2x), Gynaec (1.05x) and improvement in Anti-infectives.

• 🌟 Key brands delivered strong growth, including Telmikind (+21%), Lipirose (+30%), Statpure (+31%), Glizid (+29%), while BSV brands Foligraf (+39%), Humog (+39%) and Anti-D (+23%) performed strongly.

• 🏆 Mankind maintained its #1 prescription rank in India for the 9th consecutive year, with a 15.2% prescription share.

MANKIND PHARMA Q1: STRONG DOMESTIC GROWTH, MARGINS EXPAND 💊📈

• 📊 Revenue grew ~13% YoY, while EBITDA margin expanded 250 bps to 26.3%.

• 🇮🇳 Domestic business (excluding Consumer Healthcare) grew 11% YoY, led by 15.8% growth in Chronic therapies, including Cardiac (+19.4%) and Anti-diabetes (+12.7%).

• 🩺 Acute portfolio recovery was driven by strong performance in Gastro, VMN and Gynaecology.

• 🚀 BSV domestic specialty business delivered strong double-digit growth.

• 🛍️ OTC business grew ~4%, while International business surged 29% YoY.

• 💼 Management highlighted disciplined execution and stronger business fundamentals, positioning the company for sustainable long-term growth.

GLOBAL HEALTH (MEDANTA): EXPANDS GUWAHATI HOSPITAL PLAN TO 650 BEDS 🏥📈

• 🏗️ Board approved the revised construction plan for the upcoming Guwahati hospital, increasing capacity from 400 beds to 650 beds.

• 💰 Estimated project cost stands at ₹970 crore, funded through a mix of internal accruals and debt.

• ⏳ The expanded capacity will be added in phases over the next 3–4 years.

• 🌍 The hospital will strengthen Medanta's presence in Northeast India, serving 50+ million people across Assam and neighbouring states.

• 🩺 The facility will offer 20+ super-specialties, including transplants and advanced robotic surgeries.

• 🏥 Medanta's existing hospital network currently has a capacity of 3,737 beds across multiple cities.

🟢 Impact: Positive (Higher bed capacity expands long-term growth potential and strengthens Medanta's healthcare footprint in Northeast India.)

A weak quarter that the QoQ figures flatter — read it YoY, where the story is flat revenue and falling margins, partly (but not entirely) explained by a one-off asset write-off. Go Fashion is the women's bottom-wear retailer (Go Colors brand), a leased-store network, so like Westlife its P&L is heavily shaped by lease accounting.

The most striking line is revenue: essentially dead flat YoY (₹222.84 Cr vs ₹222.83 Cr, +0.004%). For a store-expanding apparel retailer, zero same-period growth is a genuine concern — it means new stores added over the year were offset by same-store-sales decline, i.e. negative SSSG. That's the core operating signal and it's not good. The +13.6% QoQ is just seasonality (Q4 March is a seasonally weaker quarter for this business), not momentum.

EBITDA fell 11.3% YoY with the margin dropping ~350bps to 27.35%. Part of this is the ₹6.46 Cr PP&E write-off from store consolidation sitting in other expenses — strip that out and EBITDA would be ~₹67.4 Cr, margin ~30.2%, roughly flat versus last year's 30.85%. So the underlying operating margin held up better than the headline; the reported EBITDA decline is largely the one-off write-off plus flat revenue giving no operating leverage. Still, "margin held flat on zero revenue growth after a store-cull write-off" is a soft quarter however you frame it.
The cost structure: cost of materials plus purchases plus inventory change came to ₹64.05 Cr on ₹222.84 Cr — 28.7% — versus ₹79.28 Cr / 35.6% last year, so gross margin actually improved meaningfully (~690bps). But that gross gain was eaten by higher operating costs as a share of revenue — employee cost 20.1% (from 19.8%) and other expenses 15.5% (inflated by the write-off) — on a flat top line. Good gross margin, no operating leverage because revenue didn't grow.

Below EBITDA, this is the lease-accounting compression again. Depreciation of ₹34.61 Cr (up 7.3% YoY) and finance costs of ₹12.70 Cr (up 6.0%) — together ₹47.31 Cr — consume most of the ₹60.94 Cr EBITDA. These are largely right-of-use asset depreciation and lease-liability interest, i.e. rent in disguise for the leased store estate. They keep growing with the store count even when revenue doesn't, which is exactly why PBT fell 25.8% (a steeper drop than EBITDA's 11%): flat/lower EBITDA minus rising lease charges. The store consolidation (closing/writing off underperforming stores) is management responding to this — trimming the estate — but it hit this quarter's P&L via the write-off.
The QoQ profit figures (+112% PBT, +108% PAT) are almost meaningless — Q4 was a seasonal trough with PBT of only ₹10.40 Cr, so any normal quarter looks like a huge jump off it. Don't read momentum into them.

Tax is clean: effective rate 25.0% vs 25.0% YoY — no distortion — so PAT's 25.9% decline tracks PBT's 25.8%.
No minority interest (standalone, wholly-owned). EPS of ₹3.14 vs ₹4.12 YoY is comparable (₹10 face value) — a real 24% decline, reflecting the flat revenue and lease-cost drag.

FY26 full-year context: revenue ₹838.01 Cr, PBT ₹79.04 Cr, PAT ₹59.32 Cr. This quarter's revenue run-rate is broadly in line with the prior year — again confirming the growth stall.

Bottom line: a soft quarter — flat YoY revenue (implying negative same-store-sales), EBITDA down 11% and PBT down 26%, with a ₹6.46 Cr store-consolidation write-off and rising lease-related depreciation/interest compressing the bottom line. Adjusting for the write-off, the underlying operating margin roughly held, so this is more a growth-stall story than a margin-collapse one. The QoQ improvement is pure seasonality and should be ignored. What to watch in Q2: same-store-sales growth specifically (the flat revenue is the real worry), whether the store consolidation is finished or more write-offs follow, net store additions, and whether revenue growth resumes — because with lease depreciation and interest rising every quarter, flat revenue steadily erodes PBT.

What Jyothy Labs, Page Industries and Varun Beverages tell us about the moats we don't actually own? 

On 9 May 2026, the board of Jyothy Labs met and concluded there was no further reasonable certainty that Henkel would renew the Pril and Fa brand licences beyond 31 May.

On 21 May 2026, Varun Beverages signed a revised exclusive bottling and trademark licence with PepsiCo, pushing the term from April 2039 out to April 2049 and deleting the clause that had confined VBL to acting as a special purpose vehicle for PepsiCo's business

Twelve days. Same market. Same underlying legal structure a foreign brand owner, an Indian operating partner, a fixed-term licence with defined exit provisions.

This tells one thing about the risk that one should continously think through while reading this businesses? 

Will the outcome be something like what happened with Jyothy Labs or VBL. Let's understand this case studies and then the framework to think around such businesses..

text:
Jefferies on HUL

Buy, TP Rs 2850

While HUL's 1Q was a slight miss, 7% share price drop is baffling given extent of miss.

There were a few weak spots (Home Care margins; growth in Personal Care & Foods), but offsetting factors meant the overall miss in EBITDA was small.

Also note consistent improvement in growth & profitability over past few qtrs.

Mgmt. commentary was reasonable, with expectations of stable demand & margin remaining in the guided range.

Macquarie on Chola Invest

U-P, TP Rs 1495

Delivered a strong 1Q FY27, with PAT rising 46% YoY to Rs16.5bn, broadly in line with estimates.

Better cost-to-income of 36% (vs 40% MQe) offset softer-than-expected 8.2% NIM (vs 8.5% MQe).

Credit cost was broadly in line, while AUM grew 22% YoY, led by LAP, SBPL, and SME.

RoA expanded 50bps YoY to 2.8%.

Despite decent performance, valuation remains stretched at a 3.4x FY28E P/BV, assuming 2.7% ROA

CLSA on Chola Invest

O-P, TP Rs 1970

3% PAT beat vs estimates in 1QFY27, driven by a 5% PPOP beat, partly offset by higher-than-expected credit costs.

Overall, it was a good quarter.

Disbursement and AUM growth both were in the low-20s while NIM was largely stable on a sequential basis.

Stronger-than-expected fees and lower-than-expected opex helped drive the beat on PPOP.

Asset quality improved with the calculated net slippage ratio declining 40bps YoY to 2.5% driven by an improvement in vehicle finance and CSEL; there is room for further reduction as it is still above 1QFY25 levels.

Management sounded confident on the analyst call.

HSBC on Chola Invest

Buy, TP Rs 2140

1Q underscored by healthy AUM growth, margin trends, and strong asset quality

Raise EPS by 0.9/3.1/7.9% for FY27/28/29e respectively as raise AUM growth, NIM & lower credit costs

CIFC looks attractive relative to peers & trades at 3.3x FY28e BVPS / 17.5x EPS, a discount of 19% in PB / 17% in PE to BAF

JPM on Varun Beverages

Neutral, TP Rs 530

Management tried to address key investor concerns, though a few pressure points remain visible.

Even as domestic volume growth is trending 20%+ in most months, weather-related disruptions can still weigh on reported growth, as witnessed in Q2 (April flat).

Management sounded confident of sustaining healthy double-digit growth, though delivery is increasingly reliant on sharper Rs20 propositions and scale-up of adjacencies

Competitive intensity remains elevated, particularly at lower price points (aiding category expansion), and VBL is prioritizing profitable growth over aggressively chasing low-margin Rs10 volumes.

International territories continue to fare well, led by broad-based Africa momentum, though Twizza integration/scale-up and Kenya expansion (post acquisition) will be key watch points.

VBL trades at 39x/34x CY27/28E P/E
Although see limited downside at current levels, domestic volume growth delivery (1HCY26 2 yr CAGR +~8%) will be a key share price catalyst.
Mirae Asset Sharekhan Morning Tiger ( Pre - Market Insight ) - 29th July 2026.pdf

CITI on Varun Beverages

Buy, TP cut to Rs 580 from Rs 640

India volumes grew 14% (off a -7% base) primarily impacted by weather-led disruption in April.

Key investor debate at VBL remains whether growth trajectory has structurally moderated amid increased competitive intensity in India; note that despite competitive pressures, India volumes delivered an 8% CAGR over past two years in 1HCY26.

Going ahead, while mgmt. commentary remains constructive, calling out sustained 20%+ volume growth trends extending into July, note that 2H accounts for only 35% of annual volumes. 

Believe category remains attractive (penetration-led growth opportunity) over long-term & competitive intensity could be gradually easing with Campa reducing volumes in its Rs10 SKU – we would look for an acceleration in 2-year CAGR trajectory.

CITI on SAIL 

Sell, TP Rs 160 

1Q EBITDA rose 72% yoy largely on higher realizations (+13%); volumes fell 9%, costs rose 4%. 

Adj EBITDA/t: Rs10,715 vs. Rs8,280 in 4Q; Rs5,695 last year. 

QoQ EBITDA/t move – higher realizations (Rs5,870/t), offset by higher costs (~Rs3,430). 

Call highlights: 

1) 1Q volumes fell ~9% yoy -planned shutdowns, SAIL is maintaining FY27 volume target at ~13%. 

2) July flats prices at Rs56,900 vs. Rs57,200 in 1Q; longs at Rs54,200 vs. Rs57,100. 

3) Coking coal higher qoq in 1Q, SAIL expects a reduction in Aug/Sep. 

4) 1Q wage costs rose on VRS, wage revision due in Jan27. 

5) SAIL is targeting cost savings by FY29. 6) Net debt Rs217bn, FY27/28 capex Rs150bn/Rs200bn

 Sell: (1) Likely downside to EBITDA/t – domestic weakness + limited China upside, 

(2) Limited growth potential, next leg of capacities after 3 years, 

(3) Estimate net D/EBITDA at 2.5x+ by FY28.

CLSA on Supreme Ind

Hold, TP Rs 4000

Q1 in-line , as weak sales volumes (-14% YoY) were partly offset by higher margins (on a better mix).

Management maintained its FY27 guidance of 12%-13% volume growth & a 14%-14.5% Ebitda margin

This looks demanding, despite recovering PVC prices, given ask rate for the rest of year is 20%+ on a high base.

🚨 Capri Global starts FY27 with a strong quarter.

Some numbers that stood out:

📌 Net Profit doubled YoY to ₹353 Cr
📌 AUM crossed ~₹40,000 Cr with 62% growth
📌 ROAE improved to 19.1%

Branch network now at 1,433, loan book remains 100% secured and collateralised.

Profit growth outpacing AUM growth points to improving unit economics and scale.

__Shared for informational purposes only. Not investment advice.__

CITI on Supreme Ind

Sell, TP Rs 3150

1Q EBITDA was up 25% yoy despite 14% lower volumes (channel destocking) on higher EBITDA margins (14.6% vs 12.2% in 1QFY26).

EBITDA margin improvement was likely driven by a combination of lower cost PVC inventory, better product mix, and inventory loss recorded in 1QFY26.

Plastic piping segment volumes were down ~15% yoy, EBIT/kg was Rs16.3/kg vs 19.9/kg in 4Q and Rs10.6/kg in 1QFY26.

Looking ahead, mgmt. has reiterated their guidance for 15-17% volume growth in the plastic piping segment (12-13% overall).

This implies a 26% yoy volume growth in piping segment for balance 9MFY27.

Considering modest growth indicated by mgmt. for May/Jun (in a relatively stable PVC price environment), think there could be downside risk to the FY27 volume guidance.

GS on L&T

Buy, TP Rs 4370

L&T's P&M (core) order inflow was 17% yoy in 1QFY27 (vs. GSe of -6%), and 1Q core EBITDA margins came in at 6.9% (vs. GSe of 7.1%) a 20bps decline yoy, driven by lower execution in core segments.

Key highlights from quarter:

1) Prospect base being resilient at Rs15tn despite strong order inflow in Q1 and well spread across domestic as well as international with private sector representing 45% in the mix.

2) Project execution continued to be impacted amid West Asia conflict, reflected in weaker execution;

3) FY27 guidance maintained at +10-12% on order inflows and similar growth in revenue with core margins flat (7.8% excluding realty biz. and 8.2% including realty).

Mgt highlighted that award and tendering in ME continues.

Jefferies on L&T

Buy, TP Rs 5000

Q1 EBITDA was 8% lower than expectations as E&C execution was weak.

14% YoY rise in order flow is tracking L&T’s annual 10-12% YoY growth guidance.

Management maintained its annual 10-12% YoY revenue guidance, implying that 2H will be better, but likely conditional on war settling down

Believe L&T stock should see a leg up to Rs4278 (when conflict started) if global tensions ease, with earnings visibility adding to upside thereon.

AGI Infra Limited: FY32 Vision Is Built on Scale

📍Completed Projects
AGI Infra has already completed 10 projects with a saleable area of 95.19 lakh sq. ft.

📍Ongoing Projects
The next leg is even bigger.
It currently has 12 ongoing projects with a saleable area of 168.26 lakh sq. ft.
That means the ongoing portfolio alone is nearly 1.8x the completed base.

📍Upcoming Projects
On top of that, AGI Infra has 4 upcoming projects with a saleable area of 78.73 lakh sq. ft.

📍What this means for future scale
Completed base: 95.19 lakh sq. ft.
Ongoing + Upcoming pipeline: 246.99 lakh sq. ft.

So, the future pipeline is about 2.6x the size of the completed portfolio — which clearly shows the scale of growth the company is building toward.

• 26 total projects

text:
India Built a Phone Export Industry. Now It Needs Customers It Doesn't Have.

India's handset export scheme is aimed at a global market where roughly 61% of units sit outside Apple and Samsung and are served by Chinese brands using Chinese assemblers. The binding constraint is therefore anchor customer access, not incentive quantum or installed capacity, which is why the same policy tool that worked domestically may not repeat offshore. 

This is falsified if a non Apple Indian assembler announces a multi year export contract with a top ten global brand.
